title: Formal smoothness of power series over a characteristic-zero field or Cohen ring
statement: Let $n\ge0$. In either of the following cases, put $R=\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and let $\mathfrak m_R$ be its maximal ideal: (i) $\Lambda$ is a field of characteristic zero, with $\mathfrak m_R=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$; (ii) $\Lambda$ is a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] of residue characteristic $p>0$, with $\mathfrak m_R=(p,X_1,\ldots,X_n)$. Then $\mathbf Z\to R$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_R$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]: for every commutative ring $D$, ideal $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, and ring map $g:R\to D/J$ such that $g(\mathfrak m_R^r)=0$ for some $r\ge1$, there is a ring map $h:R\to D$ with $h\bmod J=g$ and $h(\mathfrak m_R^{2r})=0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs), clauses (1) and (3) and proof. Clause (1) states formal smoothness over Q; the Z-version uses the localization Z to Q, whose square-zero lifting property is lem-weil-pbc-localization-square-zero-lifting, and the fact that units lift through square-zero quotients.

proof.text: *The test datum.* Fix $n\ge0$, $\Lambda$ and $R=\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] with $\mathfrak m_R$ as in case (i) or (ii). Every commutative ring $D$ is a $\mathbf Z$-algebra in exactly one way, and a homomorphism of $\mathbf Z$-algebras is the same as a ring homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. So, by [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] for $\varphi:\mathbf Z\to R$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_R$, the assertion is: for every commutative ring $D$, ideal $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, quotient map $q:D\to D/J$, and ring map $g:R\to D/J$ with $g(\mathfrak m_R^r)=0$ for some $r\ge1$, there is a ring map $h:R\to D$ with $q\circ h=g$; and moreover such an $h$ satisfies $h(\mathfrak m_R^{2r})=0$. Fix such $D,J,q,g,r$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Definition Tag 07EB (definition-formally-smooth) as made explicit in def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic; Lemma Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs), statement

proof.text: *Case (ii).* Here $\Lambda$ is a Cohen ring with residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], $R=C=\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ and $\mathfrak m_R=(p,X_1,\ldots,X_n)=\mathfrak m_C$. Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-cohen-formally-smooth-adic] says that $C$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Z$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology. Applied to the datum of Step 1 ($D$ with its unique ring map $\mathbf Z\to D$, $J$, $q$, $g$, $k=r$; $g$ is a homomorphism of $\mathbf Z$-algebras by Step 1), it gives a homomorphism of $\mathbf Z$-algebras, i.e. a ring map, $h:R\to D$ with $q\circ h=g$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs), clause (3)

proof.text: *Case (i): $D$ is a $\mathbf Q$-algebra compatibly with $g$ (the passage from $\mathbf Z$ to $\mathbf Q$).* Here $\Lambda$ is a field of characteristic $0$, so the ring map $\mathbf Z\to\Lambda$ is injective and every nonzero integer is a unit of $\Lambda$; hence there is a unique ring map $\iota:\mathbf Q\to\Lambda\subseteq R$, and $R$ is a $\mathbf Q$-algebra through $\iota$ (this is the $\mathbf Q$-algebra structure of part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-cohen-formally-smooth-adic]). The map $\lambda_0:\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q$, $a\mapsto a/1$, is a localization of $\mathbf Z$ at the multiplicative subset $W=\mathbf Z\setminus\{0\}$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-square-zero-lifting]: (a) $\lambda_0(s)=s$ is a unit of $\mathbf Q$ for $s\ne0$; (b) every rational number is $a/s=\lambda_0(a)\lambda_0(s)^{-1}$ with $a\in\mathbf Z$, $s\in W$; (c) $\lambda_0(a)=0$ means $a=0$, so $1\cdot a=0$ with $1\in W$. The composite $g\circ\iota:\mathbf Q\to D/J$ is a ring map, hence a homomorphism of $\mathbf Z$-algebras for the unique $\mathbf Z$-algebra structures (Step 1). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-square-zero-lifting] with $R=\mathbf Z$, $W$, $R'=\mathbf Q$, the $\mathbf Z$-algebra $D$, $N=J$ (square zero), $q$, and $g\circ\iota$: there is a ring map $\mu:\mathbf Q\to D$ with $q\circ\mu=g\circ\iota$. (This is the formal smoothness half of the formal \'etaleness of the localization $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q$, Algebra Lemma Tag 04EG.) Make $D$ a $\mathbf Q$-algebra through $\mu$; then $D/J$ is a $\mathbf Q$-algebra through $q\circ\mu=g\circ\iota$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and $g$ is a homomorphism of $\mathbf Q$-algebras since $g\circ\iota$ is exactly the structure map of $D/J$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04EG (lemma-localization-formally-etale): $R\to S^{-1}R$ is formally \'etale; used with More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07EF (lemma-compose-formally-smooth, proof omitted in the source: composing $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q$ with $\mathbf Q\to R$), written out in Steps 3-4

proof.text: *Case (i): the lift.* In case (i), $R=\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ with $\Lambda$ a field of characteristic $0$ and $\mathfrak m_R=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$, which is $C$ and $\mathfrak m_C$ of part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-cohen-formally-smooth-adic] (with $K=\Lambda$, $x_i=X_i$): $C$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Q$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Apply this to the $\mathbf Q$-algebra $D$ of Step 3 (structure map $\mu$), the ideal $J$ with $J^2=0$, $q$, and the homomorphism of $\mathbf Q$-algebras $g:R\to D/J$ (Step 3) with $g(\mathfrak m_R^r)=0$, $k=r$: there is a homomorphism of $\mathbf Q$-algebras $h:R\to D$ with $q\circ h=g$; in particular $h$ is a ring map.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs), clause (1), composed with Step 3 as in Lemma Tag 07EF (lemma-compose-formally-smooth)

proof.text: *The bound $h(\mathfrak m_R^{2r})=0$.* In both cases $h:R\to D$ is a ring map with $q\circ h=g$. For $a\in\mathfrak m_R^r$, $q(h(a))=g(a)=0$, so $h(a)\in J$. The ideal $\mathfrak m_R^{2r}=\mathfrak m_R^r\mathfrak m_R^r$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] consists of finite sums $\sum_j a_jb_j$ with $a_j,b_j\in\mathfrak m_R^r$, and $h(\sum_ja_jb_j)=\sum_jh(a_j)h(b_j)\in J^2=0$. Hence $h(\mathfrak m_R^{2r})=0$, and by Step 1 $\mathbf Z\to R$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_R$-adic topology in the explicit form stated.

lean.statement: theorem field_cohen_power_series_formally_smooth {Λ : Type u} [CommRing Λ] (n : ℕ) (m : Ideal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ)) (hΛ : (IsField Λ ∧ CharZero Λ ∧ m = Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin n ↦ (MvPowerSeries.X i : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ)))) ∨ (∃ p : ℕ, IsCohenRing p Λ ∧ m = Ideal.span (insert (MvPowerSeries.C (p : Λ)) (Set.range (fun i : Fin n ↦ (MvPowerSeries.X i : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ)))))) : Algebra.FormallySmoothAdic ℤ (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ) m ∧ ∀ (D : Type v) [CommRing D] (J : Ideal D), J ^ 2 = ⊥ → ∀ (g : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ →+* D ⧸ J) (r : ℕ), 1 ≤ r → (∀ x ∈ m ^ r, g x = 0) → ∃ h : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ →+* D, (Ideal.Quotient.mk J).comp h = g ∧ ∀ x ∈ m ^ (2 * r), h x = 0
